top_story: Iran’s renewed closure of the Strait of Hormuz on 18 April, enforced by IRGC fire on a tanker and tied explicitly to ending the US blockade of Iranian ports, marks an escalation from Tehran’s 23 March warning that threats to its power grid would trigger wider regional retaliation. That sequence sharpens the risk that a shipping crisis in the Gulf will spill into broader confrontation, with energy flows, commercial traffic, and civilian livelihoods across the region exposed to coercive disruption. In south Lebanon, the return of tens of thousands of displaced residents after the ceasefire is colliding with continued Israeli shelling and demolition activity, leaving people to re-enter damaged communities under direct threat. The combined picture is of a region where military pressure is increasingly applied through civilian infrastructure and movement, making any formal de-escalation fragile and socially costly.
